title: Get Rid Of
subtitle: 「去掉／擺脫／丟掉／取消」，要先分清是在移除物件、徹底消除問題、廢除制度、處理廢物，還是逐步淘汰某種做法。
description: 「去掉／擺脫／丟掉／取消」，要先分清是在移除物件、徹底消除問題、廢除制度、處理廢物，還是逐步淘汰某種做法。

words.example: Please remove any unnecessary files before submitting the folder.
words.exampleZh: 提交資料夾前，請移除任何不必要的檔案。

exercises.original: Please get rid of any unnecessary files before submitting the folder.
exercises.zh: 提交資料夾前，請移除任何不必要的檔案。
exercises.upgrade: Please remove any unnecessary files before submitting the folder.

options.explanation: files are simply being taken out of the folder, so remove is the neutral precise verb。
avoid means not interacting with the files, not deleting or taking them away。
replace would require substitute files。
lose suggests accidental loss。
destroy is much stronger than necessary。
clean the folder does not specifically mean taking files out.

exercises.original: The editor got rid of several paragraphs from the draft.
exercises.zh: 編輯從草稿刪去幾段文字。
exercises.upgrade: The editor removed several paragraphs from the draft.

options.explanation: paragraphs are being taken out of a text, so remove is natural。
replace would require new paragraphs in their place。
avoid does not alter the draft。
lose sounds accidental。
destroy is too strong for editing。
cleaned is not the standard verb for removing paragraphs.

exercises.original: We need to get rid of the barrier at the entrance.
exercises.zh: 我們需要移除入口的障礙物。
exercises.upgrade: We need to remove the barrier at the entrance.

options.explanation: physical barrier being taken away remove。
avoid would leave the barrier in place。
lose is accidental。
replace necessarily would require a substitute barrier。
destroy necessarily is stronger and may damage it rather than simply move it。
clean is unrelated to taking it away.

words.example: The new process is designed to eliminate unnecessary delays.
words.exampleZh: 新流程旨在消除不必要的延誤。

exercises.original: The new system should get rid of unnecessary delays.
exercises.zh: 新系統應消除不必要的延誤。
exercises.upgrade: The new system should eliminate unnecessary delays.

options.explanation: the aim is to remove delays entirely from the process, so eliminate is precise。
throw away applies to physical unwanted objects。
lose is accidental。
clean does not fit delays。
replace changes one thing for another。
avoid may reduce exposure to delays but does not necessarily remove them from the system.

exercises.original: Better checks can get rid of many common errors.
exercises.zh: 更好的檢查可消除很多常見錯誤。
exercises.upgrade: Better checks can eliminate many common errors.

options.explanation: errors being removed from a process or output fits eliminate。
discard would mean throwing away an object/version after the error occurs。
lose is accidental。
replace does not necessarily remove the underlying errors。
avoid can prevent some errors but is less direct here。
clean is not the normal verb for errors.

exercises.original: Automation may get rid of the need for manual entry.
exercises.zh: 自動化可能消除手動輸入的需要。
exercises.upgrade: Automation may eliminate the need for manual entry.

options.explanation: eliminate the need for is a very common collocation。
throw away/discard apply to unwanted items。
lose the need is not idiomatic in this context。
clean does not fit an abstract need。
replace manual entry would require stating what replaces it.
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。

words.example: The company plans to do away with unnecessary paperwork.
words.exampleZh: 公司計劃取消不必要的文書程序。

exercises.original: The company wants to get rid of unnecessary paperwork.
exercises.zh: 公司想取消不必要的文書程序。
exercises.upgrade: The company wants to do away with unnecessary paperwork.

options.explanation: paperwork here means an administrative practice, so do away with fits institutional removal。
throw away would mean physically binning documents, not ending the process。
lose is accidental。
clean is unrelated。
avoid would leave the paperwork system in place。
destroy is unnecessarily strong.

exercises.original: The reform would get rid of the old approval rule.
exercises.zh: 改革會取消舊有審批規則。
exercises.upgrade: The reform would do away with the old approval rule.

options.explanation: ending an old rule is a natural do away with context。
discard is mainly for items/ideas, not formal rules。
lose is accidental。
clean is irrelevant。
avoid means bypassing rather than abolishing the rule。
replace only would require a new rule.

exercises.original: They hope to get rid of several unnecessary steps in the process.
exercises.zh: 他們希望取消流程中數個不必要步驟。
exercises.upgrade: They hope to do away with several unnecessary steps in the process.

options.explanation: unnecessary procedural steps can naturally be done away with。
throw away is too physical。
lose suggests accident。
clean is not the right verb。
avoid means skipping rather than formally removing them。
destroy is too strong.

words.example: Discard any damaged packaging before use.
words.exampleZh: 使用前請丟棄任何受損包裝。

exercises.original: Get rid of any damaged packaging before use.
exercises.zh: 使用前請丟棄任何受損包裝。
exercises.upgrade: Discard any damaged packaging before use.

options.explanation: unwanted damaged packaging is something to discard。
avoid leaves it present。
replace may happen later but does not itself mean dispose of the damaged packaging。
lose is accidental。
cleaning damaged packaging does not solve the issue。
abolish is for rules/systems.

exercises.original: We got rid of the old version after the update.
exercises.zh: 更新後我們棄用了舊版本。
exercises.upgrade: We discarded the old version after the update.

options.explanation: an old version no longer kept is naturally discarded。
avoid does not remove it。
lost implies accident。
cleaned is unrelated。
abolished is institutional。
phased out necessarily would imply a gradual transition, not stated.

exercises.original: The team got rid of the first idea and started again.
exercises.zh: 團隊放棄第一個構思並重新開始。
exercises.upgrade: The team discarded the first idea and started again.

options.explanation: an idea consciously rejected and no longer used can be discarded。
lost suggests forgetting/misplacing it。
avoid means not engaging with it。
cleaned does not fit ideas。
abolished is too institutional。
destroyed is too strong/metaphorical here.

words.example: Old batteries must be disposed of safely.

exercises.original: You should get rid of old batteries safely.
exercises.zh: 你應安全處理舊電池。
exercises.upgrade: You should dispose of old batteries safely.

options.explanation: old batteries require proper waste handling, making dispose of exact。
lose is accidental。
avoid does not remove them。
replace focuses on substitution rather than safe disposal。
clean is irrelevant。
abolish is for systems/rules.

exercises.original: The hospital must get rid of medical waste according to regulations.
exercises.zh: 醫院必須按規例處理醫療廢物。
exercises.upgrade: The hospital must dispose of medical waste according to regulations.

options.explanation: regulated handling of waste is exactly dispose of。
throw away casually ignores safe/legal disposal requirements。
lose is accidental。
avoid leaves the waste unresolved。
replace is irrelevant。
clean is not the same as disposal.

exercises.original: How should we get rid of these confidential documents?
exercises.zh: 我們應如何處理這些機密文件？
exercises.upgrade: How should we dispose of these confidential documents?

options.explanation: confidential documents need deliberate secure disposal。
avoid does nothing to the documents。
lose would be a security failure。
clean is not the action required。
replace is unrelated。
abolish applies to rules/systems.

words.meaning: 清走；清空；大掃除式清理
words.example: We spent the weekend clearing out the garage.
words.exampleZh: 我們週末把車房裏的雜物清走。

exercises.original: We spent the weekend getting rid of old things in the garage.
exercises.zh: 我們週末把車房裏的舊物清走。
exercises.upgrade: We spent the weekend clearing out the garage.

options.explanation: removing many unwanted things from a space is exactly clearing it out。
abolishing is for systems or laws。
eliminating is too abstract/strong for household decluttering。
avoiding does not empty the space。
losing implies accident。
replacing is substitution, not clearing.

exercises.original: She got rid of clothes she no longer wore from the wardrobe.
exercises.zh: 她把衣櫃裏不再穿的衣服清走。
exercises.upgrade: She cleared out the wardrobe and removed clothes she no longer wore.

options.explanation: wardrobe decluttering with many unwanted clothes fits clear out。
abolished is institutional。
rooted out suggests hidden harmful problems。
lost is accidental。
avoided leaves the clothes there。
replaced would require new clothes.

exercises.original: We need to get rid of all the clutter in this room.
exercises.zh: 我們需要把房內雜物清走。
exercises.upgrade: We need to clear out the room and remove all the clutter.

options.explanation: removing accumulated clutter from a room fits clear out。
abolish is for systems。
eradicate is too strong/formal for household clutter。
avoid does not clear the room。
lose is accidental。
replace is not the goal.

words.example: Don't throw away the receipt until the return period ends.
words.exampleZh: 退貨期完結前不要把收據丟掉。

exercises.original: Don't get rid of the receipt yet.
exercises.zh: 暫時不要把收據丟掉。
exercises.upgrade: Don't throw away the receipt yet.

options.explanation: a physical receipt being put in the rubbish is naturally thrown away。
abolish is institutional。
avoid does not remove it。
lose suggests accident。
replace is substitution。
root out is for hidden harmful problems.

exercises.original: He got rid of the empty box after unpacking.
exercises.zh: 拆箱後，他把空盒丟掉。
exercises.upgrade: He threw away the empty box after unpacking.

options.explanation: an empty unwanted box is a normal throw-away object。
abolished/phased out/eradicated are for systems or broader problems。
avoid leaves the box there。
lost implies accidental disappearance.
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。

exercises.original: We got rid of the spoiled food immediately.
exercises.zh: 我們立即把變壞的食物丟掉。
exercises.upgrade: We threw away the spoiled food immediately.

options.explanation: spoiled food is physically discarded, so threw away is natural。
abolished is institutional。
avoid does not remove it。
lost is accidental。
replace is not the same action。
root out is metaphorical and too strong.

words.example: The proposal would abolish the outdated requirement.
words.exampleZh: 該建議會廢除這項過時要求。

exercises.original: The proposal would get rid of the outdated requirement.
exercises.zh: 建議會廢除這項過時要求。
exercises.upgrade: The proposal would abolish the outdated requirement.

options.explanation: an official requirement being ended is exactly abolished。
throw away/discard are for objects or ideas, not formal requirements。
lose is accidental。
clean is unrelated。
avoid means bypassing rather than officially ending it.
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。

exercises.original: The government plans to get rid of the tax next year.
exercises.zh: 政府計劃明年廢除這項稅項。
exercises.upgrade: The government plans to abolish the tax next year.

options.explanation: government formally ending a tax is a classic abolish context。
discard/throw away are physical-object verbs。
clean is unrelated。
lose is accidental。
avoid means not paying/encountering it, not ending the tax.
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。

exercises.original: Campaigners want to get rid of the old law.
exercises.zh: 倡議者希望廢除舊法例。
exercises.upgrade: Campaigners want to abolish the old law.

options.explanation: ending an existing law through reform is abolish。
discard/throw away are not standard legal-policy verbs。
lose is accidental。
clean is irrelevant。
replace necessarily would require specifying a new law.
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。

words.example: The company will phase out the old software over the next year.
words.exampleZh: 公司會在未來一年逐步淘汰舊軟件。

exercises.original: The company will get rid of the old software over the next year.
exercises.zh: 公司會在未來一年逐步淘汰舊軟件。
exercises.upgrade: The company will phase out the old software over the next year.

options.explanation: over the next year directly indicates gradual withdrawal, hence phase out。
throw away is immediate physical disposal。
abolish immediately contradicts the gradual timeline。
lose is accidental。
clean is unrelated。
avoid does not end use across the company.

exercises.original: The city plans to get rid of older buses gradually.
exercises.zh: 城市計劃逐步淘汰舊巴士。
exercises.upgrade: The city plans to phase out older buses gradually.

options.explanation: gradually removing a fleet from service is precisely phase out。
discard immediately contradicts the gradual plan。
lose is accidental。
avoid/clean do not end fleet use。
eradicate is too strong and inappropriate for vehicles.
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。

exercises.original: The policy is intended to get rid of the old system in stages.
exercises.zh: 政策旨在分階段淘汰舊制度。
exercises.upgrade: The policy is intended to phase out the old system in stages.

options.explanation: in stages is a direct phase-out clue。
throw away is too physical。
lose is accidental。
clean is unrelated。
avoid leaves the system intact。
abolish at once contradicts staged removal.

words.example: The organisation introduced controls to root out fraud.
words.exampleZh: 機構引入監控措施以根除欺詐。

exercises.original: The organisation introduced controls to get rid of fraud.
exercises.zh: 機構引入監控措施以根除欺詐。
exercises.upgrade: The organisation introduced controls to root out fraud.

options.explanation: fraud is a harmful hidden practice that must be found and removed, fitting root out。
throw away is physical disposal。
lose is accidental。
replace does not address the fraud itself。
clean is too vague。
avoid only reduces exposure.

exercises.original: The review aims to get rid of bias in recruitment.
exercises.zh: 檢討旨在根除招聘中的偏見。
exercises.upgrade: The review aims to root out bias in recruitment.

options.explanation: bias can be deeply embedded and requires identifying/removing it, fitting root out。
discard/throw away do not naturally apply to systemic bias。
lose is accidental。
avoid may bypass bias rather than remove it。
replace is not the action.
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。

exercises.original: Managers were told to get rid of bad practices across the organisation.
exercises.zh: 管理層被要求根除機構內的不良做法。
exercises.upgrade: Managers were told to root out bad practices across the organisation.

options.explanation: organisation-wide harmful practices being sought and removed fits root out。
throw away is too physical。
clean is vague and non-specific。
lose is accidental。
avoid does not remove practices。
replace would require alternatives.

words.example: The programme aims to eradicate the disease in the region.
words.exampleZh: 該計劃旨在根除區內這種疾病。

exercises.original: The programme aims to get rid of the disease in the region.
exercises.zh: 計劃旨在根除區內這種疾病。
exercises.upgrade: The programme aims to eradicate the disease in the region.

options.explanation: complete removal of a disease from a region is precisely eradicate。
discard/throw away are object-disposal verbs。
lose is accidental。
clean is not the correct epidemiological verb。
avoid would only reduce exposure, not remove the disease.
本題教材沒有為此選項提供個別解釋。

exercises.original: Officials hope to get rid of the pest completely.
exercises.zh: 官員希望徹底消滅這種害蟲。
exercises.upgrade: Officials hope to eradicate the pest completely.

options.explanation: pest + completely strongly supports eradicate。
lose is accidental。
avoid does not remove the pest population。
replace is irrelevant。
discard applies to objects。
clean is too weak and imprecise.

exercises.original: The campaign seeks to get rid of corruption from the institution.
exercises.zh: 運動旨在根除機構內的腐敗。
exercises.upgrade: The campaign seeks to eradicate corruption from the institution.

options.explanation: serious systemic corruption + total-removal goal supports eradicate。
throw away is physical。
lose is accidental。
clean is vague。
avoid leaves corruption existing。
replace is not the action.

words.example: The maintenance tool can purge outdated files from the system.
words.exampleZh: 維護工具可以清除系統中的過時檔案。

exercises.original: The maintenance tool gets rid of outdated files from the system.
exercises.zh: 維護工具清除系統中的過時檔案。
exercises.upgrade: The maintenance tool purges outdated files from the system.

options.explanation: system tool removing many obsolete files fits purge。
avoid does not delete them。
lose implies accidental disappearance。
replace is substitution。
abolish is institutional。
clean only is broader and less precise about removal.

exercises.original: The database process gets rid of old records automatically.
exercises.zh: 資料庫程序會自動清除舊紀錄。
exercises.upgrade: The database process purges old records automatically.

options.explanation: automatic bulk removal of records is a standard technical purge context。
throws away is too physical/informal。
avoid does nothing to records。
lose implies accidental loss。
abolish is institutional。
phase out implies gradual cessation of use, not deletion.

exercises.original: Administrators need to get rid of obsolete data before migration.
exercises.zh: 遷移前，管理員需要清除過時資料。
exercises.upgrade: Administrators need to purge obsolete data before migration.

options.explanation: obsolete data removed thoroughly before migration fits purge。
avoid leaves the data in place。
lose is accidental。
replace is substitution。
throw away is informal/physical。
abolish applies to systems/rules.

words.example: He was determined to rid himself of the habit.

exercises.original: He wants to get rid of the habit.
exercises.zh: 他想擺脫這個習慣。
exercises.upgrade: He wants to rid himself of the habit.

options.explanation: a person deliberately freeing himself from a habit fits rid oneself of exactly。
throw away applies to physical objects。
abolish is institutional。
lose suggests accidental disappearance。
clean does not fit habits。
replace would require a new habit.

exercises.original: She tried to get rid of her fear of public speaking.
exercises.zh: 她嘗試擺脫公開演說的恐懼。
exercises.upgrade: She tried to rid herself of her fear of public speaking.

options.explanation: deliberately freeing oneself from fear fits the formal reflexive construction。
discard physically is impossible for an emotion。
lose may happen but sounds involuntary。
avoid the fear does not remove it。
clean is inapplicable。
phase out is for systems/products.

exercises.original: The company wants to get rid of its dependence on a single supplier.
exercises.zh: 公司希望擺脫對單一供應商的依賴。
exercises.upgrade: The company wants to rid itself of its dependence on a single supplier.

options.explanation: deliberately freeing itself from a dependency fits rid itself of。
throw away is physical。
lose sounds accidental。
clean is not the right verb。
abolish is too institutional for dependency。
replace only would not necessarily remove dependence.

falseSynonyms.zh: 刪除不等於所有 get rid of delete 主要指文字、檔案、數據等從系統移除。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Delete is mainly for digital or written content.

falseSynonyms.zh: 清潔不等於 get rid of clean 是清潔；可以去除污垢，但不一定把東西本身處理掉。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Cleaning may remove dirt, not necessarily the object itself.

falseSynonyms.zh: 摧毀不等於 get rid of destroy 強調破壞；get rid of 不要求把對象毀掉。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON You can get rid of something without destroying it.

falseSynonyms.zh: 失去不等於 get rid of lose 常是非自願失去；get rid of 通常帶主動想移除。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Losing something is often accidental; getting rid of it is deliberate.

falseSynonyms.zh: 避免不等於 get rid of avoid 是不接觸／避開；問題仍可能存在。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Avoiding something does not remove it.

falseSynonyms.zh: 替換不等於 get rid of replace 是用另一樣東西取代；可能包含移走舊物，但核心是替代。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Replacement focuses on substitution.

falseSynonyms.zh: eliminate 通常比 get rid of 更徹底 eliminate 常表示完全消除問題、風險或可能性。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Eliminate is stronger and more complete.

falseSynonyms.zh: 結構陷阱 可說 get rid of something 或 rid oneself of something；不能說 rid of something 單獨作一般動詞結構。
falseSynonyms.point: ENGLISH COMPARISON Use get rid of, or rid oneself of.
